title: Functorial Weil pairing and alternating polarization form
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $A,B,C$ abelian varieties over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], with dual varieties and pullback homomorphisms of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus]. For group-scheme homomorphisms [def-sc-group-scheme], pullback is additive and contravariant: $(a+b)^\vee=a^\vee+b^\vee$, $(ba)^\vee=a^\vee b^\vee$, and $1_A^\vee=1_{A^\vee}$. These identities extend $\mathbf Q$-linearly to rational homomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For each prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, put $\mathbf Q_\ell(1)=(\varprojlim_n\mu_{\ell^n}(k))\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\mathbf Q_\ell$, where $\mu_{\ell^n}(k)=\{z\in k^\times:z^{\ell^n}=1\}$ and transitions are $z\mapsto z^\ell$, using [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. This is a one-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-space. There are perfect bilinear pairings $e_{A,\ell}:V_\ell A\times V_\ell A^\vee\to\mathbf Q_\ell(1)$ [sk-def-av-tate]; perfect means each induced map to the linear dual of the other factor, with values in this line, is an isomorphism. They obey $e_{B,\ell}(V_\ell(a)x,y)=e_{A,\ell}(x,V_\ell(a^\vee)y)$ for every rational homomorphism $a:A\to B$. For every invertible sheaf $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and $\lambda=\phi_L:A\to A^\vee$, the form $e^L_\ell(x,y)=e_{A,\ell}(x,V_\ell(\lambda)y)$ is alternating. If $\lambda$ is an isogeny [def-sc-isogeny], this form is nondegenerate.

source.place: Chapter I, Remark 8.5, printed p.36; §9 opening, p.41; §13 pp.57–58, Lemma 13.1 and Proposition 13.2(a),(d): Weil pairings, passage to the inverse limit, functoriality and skew symmetry; nondegeneracy from the perfect finite Weil pairings and an isogeny on rational Tate modules.

proof.text: Take $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ in [lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus]. An abelian variety $X$ over $k$ is commutative [lem-sc-av-commutative], proper and of finite presentation over the Noetherian base, smooth and hence geometrically reduced [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], and connected, hence geometrically connected because $k$ is separably closed [lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected]; so $A,B,C$ and their geometric fibres satisfy that node's hypotheses, and on schemes its line modules are the invertible sheaves. Its dual $D_X$ represents, on $k$-schemes $T$, exactly the functor of rigidified, fibrewise algebraically trivial families that $X^\vee$ represents in [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] (same algebraic-equivalence relation, same rigidification). The Yoneda lemma gives an isomorphism $\psi_X:X^\vee\to D_X$ pulling the universal family of $D_X$ back to $\mathcal P_X$ with its rigidification. Both universal sheaves are trivial on $X\times0$, so $\psi_X(0)=0$. Apply [lem-sc-rigidity] to $G(u,v)=\psi_X^{-1}(\psi_X(u+v)-\psi_X(u)-\psi_X(v))$ on $X^\vee\times_kX^\vee$ with values in $X^\vee$ (here $X^\vee$ is proper, geometrically connected and geometrically reduced by the same two citations, and separated of finite type): $G$ maps $X^\vee\times0$ to $0$, hence $G=g\circ\mathrm{pr}_2$ with $g(v)=G(0,v)=0$. So $\psi_X$ is an isomorphism of group schemes. Since $c^\vee$ in both nodes classifies the pulled-back family $(c\times1)^*\mathcal P$, the $\psi$'s carry the duals of homomorphisms to each other. Hence the two biadditivity isomorphisms and $(c\times1)^*\mathcal P_Y\cong(1\times c^\vee)^*\mathcal P_X$ for $c:X\to Y$, axis trivializations included, hold for the duals and Poincare sheaves of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus].

source.place: I §8 Remark 8.5, p.36, and the universal Poincare sheaf of §8; §9 opening, p.41 (dual homomorphism); rigidity, I §1.

proof.text: For $a,b:A\to B$, pull the first biadditivity $(m_B,1)^*\mathcal P_B\cong p_{13}^*\mathcal P_B\otimes p_{23}^*\mathcal P_B$ of step 1 back along $(a,b,1):A\times B^\vee\to B\times B\times B^\vee$. Since $a+b=m_B\circ(a,b)$, tensor pullback [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] and the composite and identity comparisons of [def-pc-module-pullback] give $((a+b)\times1)^*\mathcal P_B\cong(a\times1)^*\mathcal P_B\otimes(b\times1)^*\mathcal P_B$, that is, by step 1, $(1\times(a+b)^\vee)^*\mathcal P_A\cong(1\times a^\vee)^*\mathcal P_A\otimes(1\times b^\vee)^*\mathcal P_A$. Pulling the second biadditivity $(1,m_{A^\vee})^*\mathcal P_A\cong p_{12}^*\mathcal P_A\otimes p_{13}^*\mathcal P_A$ back along $(1,a^\vee,b^\vee):A\times B^\vee\to A\times A^\vee\times A^\vee$ identifies the right side with $(1\times(a^\vee+b^\vee))^*\mathcal P_A$. All isomorphisms keep the axis trivializations, so the representing property of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] gives $(a+b)^\vee=a^\vee+b^\vee$ as morphisms. For $b:B\to C$, $((ba)\times1)^*\mathcal P_C\cong(a\times1)^*(1\times b^\vee)^*\mathcal P_B=(1\times b^\vee)^*(a\times1)^*\mathcal P_B\cong(1\times a^\vee b^\vee)^*\mathcal P_A$, so $(ba)^\vee=a^\vee b^\vee$; $1^*\cong1$ gives $1_A^\vee=1_{A^\vee}$. Additivity allows a unique $\mathbf Q$-linear extension on $\operatorname{Hom}\otimes\mathbf Q$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the composition and identity identities persist by expansion on pure tensors.

Put $R=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $U=\varprojlim_n\mu_{\ell^n}(k)$. Choose a primitive $\ell$th root $\zeta_1$ by [lem-sc-primitive-root]. Inductively choose $\zeta_{n+1}$ with $\zeta_{n+1}^{\ell}=\zeta_n$, using algebraic closedness [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Its order is $\ell^{n+1}$: its $\ell^{n+1}$st power is one and its $\ell^n$th power equals $\zeta_n^{\ell^{n-1}}\ne1$. Thus exponents identify each root group with $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ and the power transition with reduction. By [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property], $R\cong\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/\ell^n$: apply its universal property to the ring of compatible residues and its projections; the inverse is the residue map, and both composites are identities by coordinate equality and residue separation. Hence $U=R\zeta$ is free of rank one, and $U\otimes_R\mathbf Q_\ell$ is a one-dimensional line. The action is $(c u)_n=u_n^{c\bmod\ell^n}$; this construction is independent of the chosen basis.

Use [sk-def-av-tate] for the actual torsion-coordinate inverse limits. By [lem-sfb-finite-torsion-weil-pairing] the formula $E_A(x,y)_n=w_{A,n}(x_n,y_n)$ is a compatible root sequence, since $w_{A,n+1}(x_{n+1},y_{n+1})^\ell=w_{A,n}(\ell x_{n+1},\ell y_{n+1})=w_{A,n}(x_n,y_n)$. Finite bilinearity makes this $R$-bilinear, with scalar $c$ acting at coordinate $n$ through its residue modulo $\ell^n$. Using the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], extend it to $e_{A,\ell}$ on the rational Tate modules by
$$e_{A,\ell}(x\otimes a,y\otimes b)=E_A(x,y)\otimes ab.$$
Balancing holds because $E_A(cx,y)=cE_A(x,y)=E_A(x,cy)$; extending separately in the two tensor factors gives a unique bilinear map.

source.place: I Lemma 13.1 and the inverse-limit definition, pp.57–58; rational scalar extension written out.

proof.text: By [thm-av-final], the point groups of $A$ and $A^\vee$ are divisible and their integral Tate modules are finite free. The projection $T_\ell D\to D[\ell^n](k)$ is surjective for $D=A,A^\vee$: start with a given level-$n$ point, lift it successively under $[\ell]$ using divisibility, and define lower coordinates by multiplication by powers of $\ell$. Suppose $E_A(x,y)=0$ for all integral $y$. At level $n$, projection surjectivity and perfectness of $w_{A,n}$ in [lem-sfb-finite-torsion-weil-pairing] force $x_n=0$; hence $x=0$. Interchanging the arguments proves the other vanishing implication. These implications persist after rationalization: finite freeness identifies each Tate module with $R^r$, so a rational vector is $\ell^{-b}x$ for an integral $x$, and the maps from both the integral modules and $U\cong R$ into their rationalizations are injective. If the rational vector pairs to zero with every rational vector, evaluating on integral vectors gives $E_A(x,y)=0$ and therefore $x=0$. Trivialize $U\otimes\mathbf Q_\ell$ by the basis of step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-perfect-pairing], with finite-dimensionality from [thm-av-final], to get both isomorphisms to the linear duals. Composing with the inverse trivialization gives the required line-valued perfectness.

source.place: I §13, pp.57–58, finite nondegeneracy and passage to rational Tate modules; I §7 p.34 for Tate ranks.

proof.text: For an integral homomorphism $a:A\to B$, [lem-sfb-finite-torsion-weil-pairing] gives $w_{B,n}(a x_n,y_n)=w_{A,n}(x_n,a^\vee y_n)$ for each $n$. Thus equality of inverse-limit coordinates gives $E_B(T_\ell(a)x,y)=E_A(x,T_\ell(a^\vee)y)$, with the componentwise maps of [sk-def-av-tate]. Extend to rational vectors by the formula of step 4. Componentwise addition gives $T_\ell(a+b)=T_\ell(a)+T_\ell(b)$, so its rational action extends $\mathbf Q$-linearly as in step 2. For a rational homomorphism $a=f/N$ with $N>0$, both sides of the adjoint identity are $N^{-1}$ times the identity for $f$; every element of $\operatorname{Hom}\otimes\mathbf Q$ has such a common-denominator expression by the tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. This proves functoriality with exactly the rational dual of step 2.

source.place: I Proposition 13.2(a), p.58; rational extension by bilinearity.

proof.text: For $\lambda=\phi_L$, the finite skew identity in [lem-sfb-finite-torsion-weil-pairing] gives $E_A(x,T_\ell(\lambda)y)=-E_A(y,T_\ell(\lambda)x)$ at every coordinate (the target is now written additively). It persists on rational vectors. Taking $y=x$ gives $2e^L_\ell(x,x)=0$, hence $e^L_\ell(x,x)=0$ because $\mathbf Q_\ell$ has characteristic zero [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. This includes $\ell=2$. If $\lambda$ is an isogeny, [lem-sfb-simple-isogeny-decomposition] supplies $g$ and $N>0$ with $g\lambda=[N]_A$ and $\lambda g=[N]_{A^\vee}$. On rational Tate modules their componentwise actions therefore have composites $N\,1$, so $V_\ell(\lambda)$ has inverse $N^{-1}V_\ell(g)$. Perfectness of $e_{A,\ell}$ now gives nondegeneracy of $e^L_\ell$: vanishing in the first variable can be tested on every vector of $V_\ell A^\vee$ by this surjectivity; vanishing in the second forces $V_\ell(\lambda)y=0$ and then $y=0$. No assumption that $N$ or the isogeny degree is prime to $\ell$ is needed.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement. Derived additive duality from the universal primitive-family identity; constructed the Tate line and rational pairing coordinatewise from finite pairings; proved two-sided nondegeneracy, rational adjunction, alternation including ell=2, and isogeny nondegeneracy. Two geometric statement-only nodes and one exact Mathlib linear-algebra leaf. Maintainer review: the primitive-family node was a specialization of the existing lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus and is dropped; step 1 now identifies the two dual constructions as groups (Yoneda plus rigidity), which supplies the missing link between the group law of the dual and tensor products used for additivity.
